chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, who said:

I read in the book of Abi al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'Tell my Shia that my Ziyarah is equal in the sight of Allah to one thousand Hajj.' He said, so I asked Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'One thousand Hajj?' He said, 'Yes, by Allah, and one million Hajj for whoever visits him while knowing his rights.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam al-Rida (a.s.) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the profound spiritual merit of visiting Imam al-Rida (a.s.), equating it to a thousand Hajj pilgrimages, which expands to one million for those who possess *ma'rifah* (gnostic knowledge) of his rights. In Shia tradition, this emphasizes that the quality of devotion and theological understanding during ziyarah outweighs mere ritual performance, linking physical pilgrimage to spiritual realization.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 9. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan Al-Saffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Nasr Al-Bizanťi, who said:

I read the following in the letter of Abil Ḥasan Al-Riďā (a.s.): Tell my Shia that coming to my Ziyārah in the eyes of Allāh is equal to performing one thousand Hajj. So I asked Abā Ja’far (Imam Jawād (a.s.)), “One thousand Hajj!?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “I swear to Allah, yes! And (the reward is) one million Hajj for those who go to his Ziyārah while knowing his rights.”
